en turnering.explanation: "En turnering" means "a tournament". To say a team wins one, use the verb "at vinde" (to win): "Holdet vandt turneringen" (The team won the tournament).

en tusch.explanation: "En tusch" means "a marker". Another name for it is "en tuschpen" (a felt-tip pen), built from "tusch" and "en pen" (a pen).

en tv-kanal.explanation: "En tv-kanal" means "a TV channel". To tell someone to change the channel, say "Skift kanal" (Change the channel).

en tv-serie.explanation: "En tv-serie" means "a TV series". To count the parts of a series, use "et afsnit" (an episode): "Vi ser to afsnit i weekenden" (We watch two episodes this weekend).

en tvetydighed.explanation: "En tvetydighed" means "an ambiguity". It is the noun for "tvetydig" (ambiguous). To say something is simply unclear, use "en uklarhed" (a lack of clarity): "Der er en uklarhed i kontrakten" (There is a lack of clarity in the contract).

en tvilling.explanation: "En tvilling" means "a twin". To say two people are twins, use the plural: "Min bror og jeg er tvillinger" (My brother and I are twins).

en tvivl.explanation: "En tvivl" means "a doubt". To say you are certain, use "Der er ingen tvivl" (There is no doubt).

en type.explanation: "En type" means "a type / guy". To ask what kind of car someone has, say "Hvilken type bil har du?" (What type of car do you have?). To call someone a funny guy, say "en sjov type" (a funny guy).

en tyr.explanation: "En tyr" means "a bull". To name the star sign Taurus, use "Tyren" (the Bull): "Jeg er Tyren" (I am Taurus).

en tyrekalv.explanation: "En tyrekalv" means "a bull calf". It is built from "en tyr" (a bull) and "en kalv" (a calf). To name a young female, use "en kvigekalv" (a heifer calf): "Der er en kvigekalv i stalden" (There is a heifer calf in the barn).

en tyrker.explanation: "En tyrker" means "a Turk". The country is "Tyrkiet" (Turkey). To say something is Turkish, use "tyrkisk" (Turkish): "Jeg elsker tyrkisk mad" (I love Turkish food). Unlike English, Danish does not capitalize nationalities: "en tyrker" (a Turk).

en tysker.explanation: "En tysker" means "a German". To say your nationality, use either the noun or the adjective: "Jeg er tysker" and "Jeg er tysk" both mean "I am German".

en tyv.explanation: "En tyv" means "a thief". To say someone stole something, use the verb "at stjæle" (to steal): "Han stjal min cykel" (He stole my bike).

en tå.explanation: "En tå" means "a toe". The big toe is "en storetå" (a big toe), built from "stor" (big) and "en tå" (a toe).

en tåbe.explanation: "En tåbe" means "a fool". To say something was foolish, use "tåbelig" (foolish): "Det var tåbeligt" (That was foolish).

en tåre.explanation: "En tåre" means "a tear", as in crying. To say someone is close to crying, use "at have tårer i øjnene" (to have tears in your eyes).

en tændstik.explanation: "En tændstik" means "a match", as in a stick for lighting a fire. To say a match in sports, use "en kamp" (a game): "Vi ser en kamp i aften" (We are watching a match tonight).

en tærskel.explanation: "En tærskel" means "a threshold", as in the bottom of a doorway. To say how much pain someone can take, use "en smertetærskel" (a pain threshold): "Hun har en høj smertetærskel" (She has a high pain threshold).

en tøjbutik.explanation: "En tøjbutik" means "a clothing store". It is built from "tøj" (clothes) and "en butik" (a shop). Other shops are named the same way, such as "en skobutik" (a shoe store).

en tøjbøjle.explanation: "En tøjbøjle" means "a clothes hanger". It is built from "tøj" (clothes) and "en bøjle" (a hanger).

en tøjkurv.explanation: "En tøjkurv" means "a laundry basket". It is built from "tøj" (clothes) and "en kurv" (a basket).

en tøjstørrelse.explanation: "En tøjstørrelse" means "a clothing size". It is built from "tøj" (clothes) and "en størrelse" (a size). To ask a shop for a bigger size, say "Har I den i en større størrelse?" (Do you have it in a larger size?).

en tøjvask.explanation: "En tøjvask" means "a laundry", as in one load of clothes you wash. The business that washes clothes for you is "et vaskeri" (a laundry): "Jeg afleverer dynen på vaskeriet" (I drop the duvet off at the laundry).

en tømrer.explanation: "En tømrer" means "a carpenter". To name the person who makes furniture, use "en snedker" (a cabinetmaker): "Snedkeren laver et nyt bord" (The cabinetmaker makes a new table).

en tønde.explanation: "En tønde" means "a barrel". At Fastelavn, Danish children hit a barrel and the saying is "at slå katten af tønden" (to knock the cat out of the barrel).
